findings.title: Delete (and Pause) menu items are gated on rulerRule, so they disappear from the prom-only list view
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu still renders the Delete item only when `canDelete && rulerRule`, and the Pause item only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). This PR changes the alert list view so that `GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2` passes only `promRule` and never a ruler rule (the ruler API calls were removed on purpose). `canDelete`/`canPause` are now correctly computed from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, but the extra `rulerRule` guard means they are never used: Delete is no longer available anywhere in the alert list view even for users with delete permission, whereas before this PR the ruler rule was fetched and the action was shown. `handleDelete` only needs the identifier (`RuleActionsButtons.V2` passes `() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`), so requiring a ruler rule is unnecessary. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test actually grants AlertingRuleDelete and asserts exactly 4 menu items (no Delete), codifying the regression.

findings.title: Silence menu item is shown in the list view but clicking it does nothing because the drawer requires a rulerRule
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu now decides whether to show "Silence notifications" from the prom-rule abilities, so in the new prom-only list view (GrafanaGroupLoader / FilterView) the item is rendered when the user has silence permission. However the drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, where `rule` is the optional rulerRule prop. In the list view that prop is undefined, so `handleSilence` sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true but no drawer ever mounts and the click is a no-op. Either the menu item must be hidden when no ruler rule is available, or `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` must be able to build the silence from the prom rule. The GrafanaGroupLoader test asserts the Silence item is present but never clicks it, so this dead action is not caught.

findings.title: Grafana rule list items are rendered without a key in the .map()
findings.body: In `FilterViewResults`, `rules.map(...)` renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} .../>` for `origin === 'grafana'` without a `key`. The previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>` did pass the computed `key` (and the sibling `DataSourceRuleLoader` / `UnknownRuleListItem` branches still do). React will emit "Each child in a list should have a unique key" and fall back to index keys, so component state in the row (e.g. the open dropdown in `AlertRuleMenu`) can be attached to the wrong rule when results are appended or re-rendered. Add `key={key}` to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` branch.

findings.title: Federation detection is lost: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to a hook that hardcodes isFederated = false
findings.body: Before this change `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which made Update/Delete/Pause/Restore unsupported for federated Mimir/Metrics Enterprise rule groups (they are immutable from Grafana). It now just delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, where `const isFederated = false;` is hardcoded (with a TODO). As a result `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` (still used by the rules table and other rule-based components) will report these actions as supported for federated groups, showing Edit/Delete/Pause controls that the backend rejects. The `CombinedRule` still carries `rule.group`, so federation can still be detected; the delegation loses it.

findings.title: Prom-rule abilities restrict ModifyExport and Pause to alerting rules, dropping them for Grafana recording rules
findings.body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` sets `[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` and gates `Pause`/`Restore`/`DeletePermanently` on `isAlertingRule`, i.e. `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`. The ruler-based equivalent gates these on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule`, which is also true for Grafana-managed recording rules, and Grafana recording rules can be paused and exported. In the new list view (where only the prom-based ability is available) the Export item therefore disappears for Grafana recording rules, and Pause would be reported unsupported (currently masked by the separate `rulerRule` guard in AlertRuleMenu). Use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule` for the actions that apply to recording rules, and keep `alertingRule` only for Silence.

findings.title: Rule view links no longer carry returnTo, losing back-navigation from the rule viewer
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.GrafanaRuleListItem` built the view link with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, where `returnTo = createReturnTo()`. The new component uses `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` without the `returnTo` query parameter. The rule view page uses `returnTo` to render its back link to the page the user came from (e.g. a filtered/paginated list); without it users are sent to the default destination instead of the list they navigated from. Restore the `returnTo` parameter (the AlertRuleMenu export item still relies on this mechanism).

findings.title: Comment and variable name still describe ruler-rule preloading that was removed
findings.body: The ruler prefetch (`alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)`) was removed from `useGrafanaGroupsGenerator`, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX..." and the local variable is still called `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead future readers into thinking ruler rules are still fetched here; update the comment and rename the variable (e.g. `cachePreload`).

findings.title: No test covers Delete/Silence in the prom-only list; the new test asserts the broken behaviour
findings.body: The new "should render correct menu actions" test grants AlertingRuleDelete and per-folder delete permissions but then asserts `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` (Silence, Copy link, Duplicate, Export), i.e. it locks in the fact that Delete is missing from the prom-only list view; it also never clicks Silence even though the drawer cannot render without a ruler rule. Additionally, `RulesTable.test.tsx` mocks `useRulerRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` wholesale, so the `(ruler ability) || (prom ability)` combination logic is never exercised with real hooks, and the newly added `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`/`useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` have no direct unit tests for provisioned rules or folder-loading states. Add at least one test that grants delete/silence and verifies the actions actually work in the prom-only list.
